text: A particle P of mass 0.2 kg moves with speed 4 m s and angular speed 5 rad s in a horizontal circle
on a smooth surface. P is attached to one end of a light elastic string of natural length 0.6 m. The
other end of the string is attached to the point on the surface which is the centre of the circular motion
of P.

The ends of two light inextensible strings of length 0.7 m are attached to a particle P. The other ends
of the strings are attached to two fixed points A and B which lie in the same vertical line with A above
B. The particle P moves in a horizontal circle which has its centre at the mid-point of AB. Both strings
are inclined at 60Å to the vertical. The tension in the string attached to A is 6 N and the tension in the
string attached to B is 4 N (see diagram).
A small object of mass 0.4 kg is released from rest at a point 8 m above the ground. The object
descends vertically and when its downwards displacement from its initial position is x m the object
has velocity v m s . While the object is moving, a force of magnitude 0.2v N opposes the motion.

A particle of mass 0.3 kg is attached to one end of a light elastic string of natural length 0.8 m and
modulus of elasticity 6 N. The other end of the string is attached to a fixed point O. The particle is
projected vertically downwards from O with initial speed 2 m s .
A particle P is projected from a point O with speed V m s . At time t s after projection the horizontal
and vertically upwards displacements of P from O are x m and y m respectively. The equation of the
trajectory of P is y = 2x − .
